perItemFindings.one_line: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The delivered results are an exact fixed-completion identification criterion for the restricted positive-binary causal-star model and a complete complexity classification for its explicitly encoded robust-design problem. The hardness theorem permits a switch coordinate to guard O(L) edge copies and leaves terminal degree unbounded, so it does not establish hardness for genuinely constant-fanout local switches; the definition's statement that the promised hardness sublanguage bounds every switch guard list by a constant is therefore stale and unsupported. The TL;DR's reference to the “stated local-switch restrictions” should be narrowed to binary signed guards with unrestricted copy count. The causal significance also rests on an unusually strong protocol in which exact configuration metadata reveals the realized latent-confounding graph, while no implementation or substantive design example demonstrates that this information structure occurs in practice. These scope and evidence limitations, together with only cursory theorem-level comparison to the closest switched-separation literature, constrain the leading-econometrics paper score despite the field-level theoretical result. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

HALTED AT TRIAGE: the math panel returned `revise` and its findings were never repaired, so this note is NOT established as mathematically sound — do not bank it as downgraded on this verdict alone. Open findings: wrong-moment-display@lem:path-countermodels, ballast@thm:bounded-terminal-frontier-complete, related_work_gap@ass:semi-markovian
